comparison: Perfect agreement on ionomycin experiments (C91-C93, C105, C140-C141). Both recognize these experiments demonstrate that Ca2+ homeostasis deficits contribute but do not fully explain DCV exocytosis defects, with peer review explicitly noting 'to a lesser extent' for Ca2+ contribution.

Strong agreement on protein synthesis deficits (C94-C97, C107). Both affirm SUnSET assay findings and leucine rescue specificity. OpenEval notes lack of mTORC1 involvement; peer review highlights these findings as study strengths.

Strong agreement on integrative conclusion (C5, C13, C109, C142). Both support the quantitative dissection showing protein synthesis as primary and Ca2+ as secondary contributor. Peer review explicitly confirms this dual-mechanism conclusion.

Strong agreement on leucine rescue experiments (C98-C99, C101, C108, C152-C153). Both recognize this as a key strength. OpenEval notes failure to rescue ER morphology; peer review emphasizes rescue of both DCV release and protein synthesis defects.

Agreement on ruling out ER stress (C147-C148). OpenEval explicitly evaluates ATF4 data as supporting negative result; peer review implicitly accepts by supporting overall mechanistic conclusions without challenging ER stress exclusion.

Strong agreement on selective DCV effects without SV impairment (C31-C34, C4, C126). Both affirm rigorous demonstration. OpenEval emphasizes multiple measures; peer review notes 'compelling evidence' and 'strong' data with 'rigor.' Peer review also includes C127 and C3 not in OpenEval R2.

Agreement on DCV trafficking/transport findings (C48, C120-C123). Both accept that Rab10 does not directly regulate DCV transport. OpenEval provides detailed negative results; peer review accepts indirect mechanism without challenge.

Strong agreement on ER Ca2+ depletion findings (C80-C87, C9, C90). Both affirm ER-GCaMP6 imaging, SERCA2 reduction, and rescue experiments. Peer review confirms 'compelling evidence' of 'impaired ER-based calcium buffering.' Peer review also includes C88-C89, C103-C104, C132.

Strong agreement on proteomics approach and findings (C50-C60, C6). Both affirm mass spectrometry identification of ~5400 proteins and GO enrichment. OpenEval details statistical rigor; peer review notes dataset value and thorough assessment. Peer review also includes ER protein findings (C61-C66, C7, C106, C128).

Strong agreement on ER morphology changes (C67-C72, C8). Both affirm EM findings of reduced synaptic ER and active zone length. OpenEval notes modest magnitude; peer review provides 'compelling evidence' of 'altered ER morphology.' Peer review also includes C143.

Agreement on uncertainty of therapeutic claims (C158). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about clinical translation. Peer review does not explicitly evaluate therapeutic potential, neither affirming nor challenging it.

Agreement on ER marker and FRAP findings (C73-C78). OpenEval affirms RTN4/KDEL reduction and altered ER trafficking. Peer review implicitly accepts as part of overall ER morphology evidence without specific comment on these immunofluorescence experiments.

Strong agreement on DIV7 infection strategy and DCV fusion defects (C36-C44, C3). Both affirm this controls for developmental effects. OpenEval details NPY-pHluorin imaging and rescue; peer review notes 'cautious' strategy and 'essential controls.' Peer review also includes neurite outgrowth claims (C28, C30, C111, C113-C115).

Agreement on ER protein dysregulation (C61-C66, C7). OpenEval details selective proteomics and SERCA2 reduction; peer review affirms proteomics findings as part of comprehensive approach. Both support ER remodeling interpretation.

Agreement on cytosolic Ca2+ measurements (C88-C89, C10, C104). OpenEval notes spatial heterogeneity and modest deficits; peer review accepts as part of Ca2+ homeostasis evidence supporting overall conclusions.

Partial agreement on Rab10 knockdown and neurite outgrowth (C28, C30, C111). OpenEval focuses on knockdown validation and morphology; peer review emphasizes DIV7 strategy to separate developmental from functional effects. Both support findings but group with different claim sets.

Partial overlap on selective DCV effects. OpenEval R1 focuses on knockdown validation (C28, C30, C111); peer R1 emphasizes selective DCV vs SV effects (C3-C4, C32-C34, C126-C127). Both support independence from neurite outgrowth defects.
Minimal overlap on SV exocytosis (C31). OpenEval R2 comprehensively addresses lack of SV effects; peer R12 briefly confirms SV exocytosis unaffected. Both agree on selective DCV impairment.

Minimal overlap on differential protein synthesis dependence (C127). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct comparison between DCV and SV protein synthesis dependence. Peer review includes C127 in supported findings but does not specifically evaluate this speculation.

OpenEval identifies uncertainty in claims about differential protein synthesis dependence between DCVs and SVs (C14, C129-C131). These speculative claims are not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers, though they accept the overall selective effects on DCVs.

OpenEval rates claims about ER morphology causing ribosomal protein upregulation (C143-C144, C146) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about compensatory mechanisms. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate this causal interpretation, though they accept the ER and proteomics findings separately.

OpenEval rates STIM1-mediated mechanism claims (C137-C139) as UNCERTAIN, noting reliance on unpublished data and literature without direct testing. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate this mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval rates TrkB transport mechanism claims (C149-C151) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are based on literature but not experimentally tested in this study. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate this alternative mechanism.
